To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a Bayesian neural network trained on a large-scale dataset can be used to obtain a real-time and accurate monocular 6-DO-F visual relocalization; (2) the model uncertainty is a good indicator of localization error and can be used to detect the presence of the scene in an input image; (3) the model uncertainty can be leveraged to detect and correct for training dataset shift.

We present a robust, real-time monocular visual relocalization algorithm that is trained in an unsupervised, end-to-end fashion and obtains 2m and approximately 6 degree accuracy for very large-scale outdoor scenes.
